transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-09
Start time: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ross (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (Avalon), Liam O'Connor (Avalon), Priya Desai (Avalon), Daniel Ng (Avalon SRE)
Links referenced: POC SOW (internal) https://redwood.internal/sow, Benchmark template: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/template, Security whitepaper: https://redwood.ai/security.pdf

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya, I'm the AE on this engagement, with Ethan from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Sofia Martinez: Good, thanks Maya. Busy day but excited to get this scoped.
[00:10] Liam O'Connor: Hi all. Want to make sure we get the timeline nailed down.
[00:14] Ethan Ross: Hey, quick intro: I'm Ethan, I'll drive the benchmarks and the performance run during the POC.
[00:20] Priya Desai: Priya, security. We'll need KMS and audit logs, SOC2 artifacts.
[00:25] Maya Patel: Great. Agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, and a proposed timeline with milestones: kickoff, access/setup, mid-point review, final exec readout.

[02:10] Maya Patel: Sofia, can you start with what success looks like for Avalon?
[02:15] Sofia Martinez: Sure. Primary success is accuracy on our financial reconciliation prompts — we want <= 2% false-pos rate on flagged transactions, and secondly latency. Our product team wants p99 generation under 300ms for the online path. Also cost; we have a target of keeping inference cost under $0.005 per query on average.
[02:45] Ethan Ross: Helpful. Is the 300ms p99 for a 1K token response or shorter responses?
[02:51] Sofia Martinez: Mostly short—100 to 200 tokens. Long form is less critical.
[03:00] Liam O'Connor: To add, we need the system to handle 50 concurrent requests steady state and spikes to 200 req/s during end of month.

[04:20] Ethan Ross: Good, workload sizing then: from what I'm hearing, target steady throughput ~50 rps, burst up to 200 rps. We'll size the Dedicated pool or a hosted config with autoscale.
[04:35] Daniel Ng: For POC we'll probably run against about 250k historical queries and a live test harness that replays at different QPS. We'll share logs.

[05:10] Maya Patel: Ok, benchmarks: we'll run correctness evals on your labeled set, latency runs with representative prompts, and a cost projection using our token accounting. Ethan will own the benchmark plan.
[05:25] Ethan Ross: I will provide a runbook. Typical steps: initial model selection (we'll propose 2 variants: a high-accuracy larger model and a quantized lower-cost model), baseline runs on hosted, then Dedicated baseline, then KV cache tuning and batching tests. Note: our KV cache sometimes gets transcribed as "K-V cash" in notes, ha.
[05:55] Priya Desai: On security for the POC we need either VPC peering or a private connector and KMS integration. We cannot send PII out of region.
[06:10] Maya Patel: Understood. We can do a Private deployment in your VPC for the benchmark or use Dedicated with a VPC option. We'll include an NDA and SOC2 artifacts.

[07:30] Liam O'Connor: Timeline—what's realistic?
[07:35] Maya Patel: Proposed 4-week POC: Week 0 kickoff and access setup, Week 1 data ingest & baseline runs, Week 2 tuning and mid-point review, Week 3 final benchmarks and exec readout.
[07:50] Sofia Martinez: That's aggressive but OK. We have to carve out SRE time for VPC access.

[09:00] Ethan Ross: Detailed milestones: 
- Kickoff (2026-05-11): Confirm SOW, sign access docs.
- Access/setup (by 2026-05-14): VPC peering, service account creds, sample dataset in shared S3.
- Baseline run complete (by 2026-05-18): initial model runs and latency numbers.
- Mid-point review (week of 2026-06-02): discuss tuning, KV cache config, batching strategies, and preliminary cost estimates.
- Final exec readout (2026-06-09): show results and next-step proposal.

[10:40] Daniel Ng: For access, we will need a limited IAM role and a short maintenance window for S3 ingestion, can propose times after 5/11.

[11:15] Maya Patel: We'll send a short access checklist. Ethan, you'll need keys for the benchmark runner?
[11:20] Ethan Ross: Yes, read-only S3, VPC tunnel creds or Private endpoint, and a service account for telemetry collection. We'll only collect perf metrics; no raw PII.

[12:40] Sofia Martinez: Quick question on model fallbacks—if the Dedicated instance is saturated, can Redwood route to a smaller model automatically?
[12:50] Ethan Ross: Yes, we have smart routing and fallback policies. We can set a rule to fallback from the high-accuracy model to a quantized variant when latency breaches thresholds. There is cost/accuracy tradeoff that we'll document.

[14:05] Priya Desai: Audit logs and retention—what's the standard retention period in POC? We need at least 90 days of logs for our compliance team.
[14:15] Maya Patel: We can configure 90-day retention for audit logs, and for the POC we'll provide a short-term export of logs to your S3 if required.

[16:00] Liam O'Connor: On costs—your $0.005 per query target. How do we get to that?
[16:10] Ethan Ross: Mix of batching, KV cache, and a quantized model. Example: with 4x effective batching and prefix cache hit rates at 30-40% we usually see a 2-3x cost reduction in token costs compared to naive requests. We'll run sensitivity analysis during Week 2.

[18:30] Sofia Martinez: For the labeled accuracy set, are there special pre-processing steps? Our data has a lot of redactions and placeholders.
[18:40] Ethan Ross: We'll provide a small pre-processing script; you'll run it and send back a sanitized sample.

[20:00] Maya Patel: Any competitors or alternatives you're evaluating?
[20:05] Sofia Martinez: We're also looking at Anthropic and Vertex for managed endpoints, and an internal eval of LlamaX for on-prem.

[21:30] Ethan Ross: Noted. We'll include a short comparison table in the SOW for the POC.

[23:00] Maya Patel: Recap and next steps: Maya to send SOW and pricing by 2026-05-11; Ethan to send benchmark runbook by 2026-05-12; Avalon to share sample workload and provide VPC access by 2026-05-14. Mid-point review week of 2026-06-02; exec readout 2026-06-09.

[24:30] Priya Desai: Also please attach SOC2 and KMS integration doc.
[24:35] Maya Patel: Will do.

[26:00] Liam O'Connor: One last thing—can we do an initial smoke test in hosted mode while VPC access is being arranged?
[26:10] Ethan Ross: Absolutely. We can run a lightweight hosted baseline to validate prompts without moving data out. We just need sanitized samples.

[28:00] Maya Patel: Great. I'll follow up with calendar invites for the kickoff and mid-point, and include the SOW and runbook links. Thanks everyone.
[28:15] Sofia Martinez: Thanks, talk soon.
[28:20] Meeting end.
